title: Baseball Game Score

concept.title: Operations that look at the last scores
body: A stack is a good fit whenever the rules talk about **"the previous one"** or **"the last two"**. Here every operation reads or removes the most recent scores, which are exactly the top of a stack of scores.
Reading the top without removing it (`scores[-1]`) is called **peek** or `top`. Only `C` removes a score; `+` and `D` add a new one on top. The answer is the sum of the scores that are left.

statement: You record the scores of a game. You get a list of operations. An integer means a new score with that value. `+` records a new score equal to the sum of the previous two scores. `D` records a new score equal to twice the previous score. `C` removes the previous score from the record. Print the sum of all scores in the record after all operations.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` operations separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print the sum of the scores.
constraints: Every operation is valid: there are enough previous scores for it.
Integers are between -30000 and 30000. All scores and sums fit into 64 bits.

examples.note: Scores: 5, then 2, then C removes 2, D adds 10, + adds 5 + 10 = 15. Sum 30.

hints: Keep the recorded scores on a stack.
`+` and `D` read the top of the stack; `C` removes it.
At the end add up what is left on the stack.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
ops = input().split()
